A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ReCamMaster and contain complete, readable main text and Appendices A–C. Their equations, tables, figures, and corresponding experiments can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original quantitative comparisons, training and conditioning ablations, dataset-construction experiments, and qualitative application results.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds a noise-augmentation ablation and qualitative experiments with non-overlapping first frames.

M1.justification: The architecture, frame-dimension conditioning, camera encoder, objectives, and training strategy remain unchanged. Noise augmentation was already described in v1 Section 4.4; its new ablation does not introduce a method component.

E1.justification: Appendix C.4 adds a distinct starting-viewpoint scenario: generated and source videos need not share their first frame. It reports 27K rendered training videos and qualitative evaluation for this scenario. Existing Multi-Cam Video, WebVid, and DeepStab coverage remains.

E2.justification: Table 4 adds the '+ Add noise' training variant as an ablation comparator against the baseline and full configuration. The external comparators GCD, Trajectory-Attention, and DaS, and the channel/view conditioning alternatives, remain unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 adds a noise-only ablation control and reports using 27K training videos for the new first-frame scenario. Section 5.1 retains the original training settings, metrics, and evaluation with 1,000 WebVid videos and ten camera trajectories.

E4.justification: Table 4 newly isolates the effect of noise augmentation. Appendix C.4 and Figure 10 test generation from different initial viewpoints after using additional training data. Existing conditioning and dataset ablations and failure-case analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical significance tests for the experiments. The added results retain point-estimate and qualitative reporting.

E6.justification: Table 4 adds noise-ablation results: FID 65.17, FVD 164.04, aesthetic quality 40.36, and imaging quality 52.22. Figure 10 adds different-first-frame examples. Existing numerical entries in Tables 1–5 remain unchanged, including the full model's FID 57.10 and FVD 122.74.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and Equations 1–10 remain equivalent, including flow matching, conditioning operations, and camera-speed construction. No new theorem, proof, or substantive derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The central claims remain camera-controlled video re-rendering through frame-dimension conditioning, a realistic synchronized training dataset, superior empirical performance, and potential applications. The added experiments support these retained claims without redefining the main contribution.

C2.justification: Section 6 adds an explicit qualification that its super-resolution application enhances central patches rather than fully matching the conventional task. Appendix C.4 acknowledges the shared-first-frame condition of the main tests and interprets the added examples as evidence for broader starting-viewpoint applicability.

D1.justification: v1 provides a project page and promises a dataset release; v2 supplies an explicit repository link and reports public code and dataset availability. Appendix C.4 also newly discloses the main tests' shared-first-frame assumption. Existing implementation details and hyperparameters are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds ReconX, DimensionX, and TrajectoryCrafter, briefly expanding discussion of reconstruction from diffusion-generated videos and concurrent camera-control methods. The overall research positioning remains stable; these citations do not become new external experimental baselines.

P1.justification: v2 makes limited grammar and terminology corrections, updates the Kling Team affiliation, and lightly revises related-work prose. It inserts Appendix C.4 and moves failure-case discussion to C.5 while retaining the main section structure.

P2.justification: Table 4 gains an ablation row and changes '+ Both' to '+ All'. A new Figure 10 is inserted; the existing failure figure becomes Figure 11 and later figures are renumbered. Appendix layout changes locally, while the existing visual examples are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly strengthens empirical support through the noise ablation and different-first-frame examples, clarifies the super-resolution application's limits, and improves code/data access documentation. The gains remain limited: the new viewpoint experiment is qualitative and uses additional training data, while the main performance comparisons and uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged.
